title: C-5 — Joined record (one row per request)
description:
Emitted as Parquet by Person A's pipeline, which is a PURE FUNCTION of (manifest, three log files). No network, no engine, runnable on a laptop. Figure scripts consume Parquet only. Keeping these two stages separate means B can hand A a directory of simulator logs and A's pipeline processes them with zero changes.

THE HONEST HANDLING OF F-18: F-18 asks for transport_in and transport_out as separate stages. Without clock synchronisation across machines you CANNOT measure them separately — you can only measure the sum of everything not accounted for by single-host durations. Report it as one residual, state why, and note that on a LAN it is small enough that its decomposition does not affect any hypothesis. Do NOT install PTP to fix this; it is a week you do not have, for a number you do not need.

CLOCK DISCIPLINE (§12.3): there is NO cross-host subtraction anywhere in this schema. transport_residual_ms is named 'residual' precisely so nobody mistakes it for a measurement.

R.$comment: from manifest — heterogeneity ratio max/min node throughput

prefill_ms.$comment: from worker — null if F-18 partial

decode_ms.$comment: from worker — null if F-18 partial

transport_residual_ms.description: DERIVED: e2e_ms - queue_wait_ms - service_ms - decide_us/1000. A residual, not a measurement.

is_warmup.description: DERIVED: intended_offset_s < manifest.warmup_s — computed from the TRACE, never from run wall-clock, so warmup discard is identical in hardware and simulator runs (§12.5).
